sentences.text: So why does an hour have sixty minutes, and not a hundred?
Blame people who lived over four thousand years ago.
The Sumerians and Babylonians counted in sixties.
Sixty splits evenly into halves, thirds, quarters, fifths, and tenths.
A hundred can't even be split into thirds.
Later, astronomers used those sixties to divide up time.
Nobody knows for sure why they picked sixty, but we still count that way every time we check a clock.
